QuestionStmt.S: Identify substrate 'A' in the following reaction. $$A + CO_2 \xrightarrow[6 \text{ atm}]{398 \text{ K}} \text{Sodium salicylate} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_3O^+}} \text{Salicylic acid}$$

Solution.S:
Concept: This reaction is the Kolbe's reaction (also known as Kolbe-Schmitt reaction).

In this reaction, sodium phenoxide (C₆H₅ONa) reacts with carbon dioxide under high pressure (6 atm) and temperature (398 K) to form sodium salicylate. Upon acidification with H₃O⁺, it gives salicylic acid.

Thus, substrate A is sodium phenoxide, which corresponds to option B.
